symptom: `mxcli check script.mdl -p app.mpr` warns MDL-BE06 "the after-startup microflow Fulfilment.ASU_Startup does not reach BusinessEvents.StartupBusinessEvents, so the consumer is never started" on an app that is wired correctly and consumes every event, and the advice ("add a call to it") cannot be followed because the call is already there (ako/mxcli#2384 M4)
cause: In Business Events 3.12.1 `StartupBusinessEvents` is a **Java action** (Private/Java_Actions, javasource/businessevents/actions/StartupBusinessEvents.java); the module ships no microflow of that name. The rule's walk collected only `*microflows.MicroflowCallAction` (`calledMicroflows`) and the script-side check matched only `*ast.CallMicroflowStmt`, so a `call java action` was invisible and the rule warned on every correctly wired consumer
file: `mdl/executor/validate_business_event_consumers.go`: `calledMicroflows`/`microflowReaches` replaced by `flowCallTargets` (returns microflow AND Java action targets) and `microflowStartsBusinessEvents`; `flowCallsStartupBusinessEvents` also matches `*ast.CallJavaActionStmt`; warning text now names `call java action`. Tests `mdl/executor/validate_business_event_consumers_test.go`
insight: **The test fixture invented the dependency's shape, so the blindness was undetectable.** `beFixture` built a MICROFLOW named StartupBusinessEvents and had ASU_Startup call it as one; every BE06 test passed while the rule warned on every real app. The marketplace module's shape is not mxcli's to assume — reading the shipped .mpk (BusinessEvents_3.12.1.mpk, already in the repo) settles it in one command: `find javasource -name '*.java'` lists seven Java actions including StartupBusinessEvents, and the module .mpr has no microflow of that name. Rule: when a check asserts something about a marketplace module, build the fixture from the module artefact, not from a guess. Both shapes are now accepted (Java action, or a microflow of that name) because the module is a dependency whose shape can change between versions, and accepting only the new one would reintroduce the false warning on an older version. Control: reverting the walk to microflow-only fails the clean-fixture silence test with the reporter's exact message, which it could not do before the fixture was corrected. Measured while here (same .mpk): one `executeAction()` logs BOTH "Business events started successfully" and the module-running-mode line, so that pair appearing twice means the action ran twice, not that the module self-starts; the jar's META-INF/services holds only Kafka's ConfigProvider and SLF4J's provider, i.e. no Mendix auto-start SPI; and `StartupService.init` initialises EventRateMetricsService, LogCollectorService and HeartbeatService — NOT consumer subscriptions — while `HeartbeatService.init` creates a new ScheduledExecutorService and overwrites the static `pulseThread` without shutting the old one down, so a duplicate call leaks a pool and doubles the heartbeat
